name: ADT7410 precision temperature sensor
description: Analog Devices 16-bit digital temperature sensor (−55 to 150 °C, ±0.5 °C from −40 to 105 °C at 3 V; 0.0078 °C resolution in 16-bit mode) with an I2C interface. Runs on 2.7–5.5 V. Sold as: Adafruit ADT7410 High Accuracy I2C Temperature Sensor Breakout (#4089, STEMMA QT version; 6-pin: VIN, GND, SCL, SDA, INT, CT), I2C address 0x48 (0x49–0x4B with the A0/A1 jumpers on the back).
eli5: A very accurate thermometer chip that tells your board the temperature to a fraction of a degree.

pins.name: VIN
pins.description: Supply 2.7–5.5 V, goes straight to the chip (no regulator) and to the 10 kΩ I2C pull-ups: use 3.3 V with a 3.3 V board

pins.name: SCL
pins.description: I2C clock (10 kΩ pull-up to VIN on the board)

pins.name: SDA
pins.description: I2C data (10 kΩ pull-up to VIN on the board)

pins.name: INT
pins.description: Over/under-temperature interrupt output, open-drain, active low by default (10 kΩ pull-up on the board); not needed for basic use

pins.name: CT
pins.description: Critical-temperature output, open-drain, active low by default (10 kΩ pull-up on the board); not needed for basic use

supplierQuery: Adafruit ADT7410 I2C temperature sensor breakout 4089
buildNotes: Power VIN from 3.3 V when using an ESP32 or Pico: the board's SDA/SCL pull-ups go to VIN, so 5 V on VIN would put 5 V on the microcontroller's pins.
The temperature is in registers 0x00 (MSB) and 0x01 (LSB), twos complement; read both bytes in one transfer starting at 0x00.
Power-up default is 13-bit (0.0625 °C, low 3 bits are alarm flags); write 0x80 to configuration register 0x03 for 16-bit mode, where °C = signed code / 128.
A conversion takes about 240 ms in continuous mode, so wait at least that long after changing the configuration.
Default address 0x48; close the A0 and/or A1 jumpers on the back for 0x49, 0x4A or 0x4B.
Keep the sensor away from the regulator and the microcontroller, which warm the air around them.

driver.code:
# ADT7410 16-bit I2C temperature sensor (Analog Devices), MicroPython driver.
# Written from the ADT7410 data sheet Rev. C: register 0x00/0x01 = temperature MSB/LSB
# (twos complement, MSB first, pointer auto-increments), 0x03 = configuration,
# 0x0B = ID (bits 7:3 = 11001). 16-bit mode: T = code / 128 (code signed);
# 13-bit mode: T = (code >> 3) / 16, bits 2:0 are TCRIT/THIGH/TLOW flags.
import time

_REG_TEMP = 0x00
_REG_CONFIG = 0x03
_REG_ID = 0x0B


class ADT7410:
    def __init__(self, i2c, addr=0x48, high_res=True):
        self.i2c = i2c
        self.addr = addr
        if (self.i2c.readfrom_mem(addr, _REG_ID, 1)[0] & 0xF8) != 0xC8:
            raise OSError('ADT7410 not found at 0x%02X: check the wiring and A0/A1' % addr)
        self.high_res = high_res
        # Bit 7 = resolution (1 = 16-bit), bits 6:5 = 00 continuous conversion.
        self.i2c.writeto_mem(addr, _REG_CONFIG, bytes([0x80 if high_res else 0x00]))
        time.sleep_ms(250)  # a conversion takes 240 ms (typ) in continuous mode

    def temperature(self):
        """Last converted temperature in °C."""
        d = self.i2c.readfrom_mem(self.addr, _REG_TEMP, 2)
        code = (d[0] << 8) | d[1]
        if code & 0x8000:
            code -= 65536
        if self.high_res:
            return code / 128
        return (code >> 3) / 16  # arithmetic shift keeps the sign; drops the 3 flag bits

example.code:
from machine import I2C, Pin
import time
from adt7410 import ADT7410

i2c = I2C({I2C_ID}, sda=Pin({SDA}), scl=Pin({SCL}))
sensor = ADT7410(i2c)
while True:
    print('T=%.2fC' % sensor.temperature())
    time.sleep(1)
